task_definition.task_name: DAS Data Stochastic Noise Removal via Curvelet Denoising

task_description.overview: Remove stochastic noise from DAS earthquake records using curvelet transform with reference or automatic thresholding.
steps: Load the preprocessed DAS data with spikes removed and bandpassed around 1–20 Hz.
Trim the full record into earthquake windows (sec_eq) and baseline noise windows (sec_ns).
Option A (soft threshold): perform curvelet transform denoising using sec_ns as reference noise, apply default soft threshold, reconstruct waveform.
Option B (hard threshold): perform curvelet denoising using sec_ns, apply hard threshold to preserve amplitude.
Option C (automatic threshold): perform curvelet denoising without reference noise, compute coefficient inflection points to set threshold (pad=0, knee_fac adjustable).
Compare and plot the original and denoised outputs.

task_definition.agent_prompt: Read DAS data from {segy_file_path} with ch2={ch2}, set dx to {channel_spacing_dx} and start_time to {start_time}. Apply a {bandpass_freq[0]}–{bandpass_freq[1]} Hz bandpass filter and remove spikes (consider using daspy `sec.spike_removal()`). Define earthquake window from {trim_windows.eq[0]} to {trim_windows.eq[1]} and noise window from {trim_windows.noise[0]} to {trim_windows.noise[1]}. Perform curvelet denoising in three modes: soft threshold with noise reference, hard threshold with noise reference while set `soft_thresh` to false, and automatic threshold (pad={automatic_params.pad}, knee_fac={automatic_params.knee_fac}). Plot figure to show the original event data, and the denoised data in three modes. Note: 1) consder using daspy package to load, processing (e.g. bandpass filter, spike removal, curvelet denoising, etc.) and plot the data. 2) Save the denoised data to {denoised_data.save_name} with content {denoised_data.content} and the plot to {denoised_data_plot}.
